sentences.text:
K Venkatesh, Secunderabad And 4 Others vs K Venkata Swamy,
Secunderabad And Anr on 21 July, 2023
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Namavarapu Rajeshwar Rao
 M.A.C.M.A.No.2308 Of 2015
Judgment:

This MACMA is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 by the appellants/petitioners aggrieved by the order and decree dated 17.01.2015 passed in O.P.No.585 of 2013 by the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-Cum-II Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad (for short "the Tribunal") seeking enhancement of the compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-Cum-II Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties will be hereinafter referred to as they are arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows :
The petitioners filed a claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.9,00,000/- on account of the death of Smt.K.Srilatha (hereinafter referred to as 'the deceased')
stating that on 18.11.2012 at about 19.00 hours, the deceased along with her husband and children was proceeding on the motorbike from Hyderabad to Cheryal and when they reached the outskirts of Gouraram Village, one motor bike bearing No.AP-29-AA-9074, which was driven in a rash and negligent manner from their behind and dashed their motorbike, due to which, the deceased received grievous injuries and other injuries all over her body and immediately she was shifted to Gandhi Hospital, Secunderabad, where while undergoing treatment, she died.
The Police Gouraram registered a case in Cr.No.75 of 2012 against the driver of the offending vehicle.
At the time of the accident, the deceased was aged about 23 years and was hale and healthy and she used to earn Rs.7,500/- per month by doing tailoring and embroidery work.
Due to the death of the deceased, the petitioners lost their source of income.
Therefore, the petitioners filed the claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.9,00,000/-.

4. Before the Tribunal, with regard to awarding just compensation, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners relied upon the decision reported in 2013 ACJ 1403, wherein the Lordships held as follows :
"The Tribunal/Court has a duty, irrespective or the amount claimed, to award a just, equitable, fair and reasonable compensation."

5. Respondent No.2 filed a counter denying the petition allegations and mainly contended that the accident has occurred due to the negligent driving of the motorbike on which the deceased was K Venkatesh, Secunderabad And 4 Others vs K Venkata Swamy, Secunderabad And Anr on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189486482/
1 travelling.

entities.text: K Venkatesh, Secunderabad And 4 Others vs K Venkata Swamy, Secunderabad And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The deceased was aged more than 30 years, she was not doing any work and not getting income, she was only a housewife and the amount claimed by the petitioners is excessive and prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
6. To prove the case of the petitioners, the 1st petitioner himself was examined as PW.1 and got marked Exs.A1 to A5.
On behalf of respondent No.2, no oral evidence was adduced, but Ex.B1-copy of the insurance policy was marked.

7. After considering the oral and documentary evidence available on record, the Tribunal held that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and accordingly, awarded an amount of Rs.7,13,500/- with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization to be paid by the respondent Nos.1 and 2.

Challenging the same,
the present appeal is filed by the petitioners seeking enhancement.

8. Heard both sides and perused the record.
9.

Learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that though the deceased was earning Rs.7,500/- per month by doing tailoring and embroidery work, the Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.4,500/- per month, which is very meager.
The Tribunal has not awarded just compensation under other heads and therefore, the amount awarded by the Tribunal is very meager and unjustifiable.

10. Learned Counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent/Insurance Company submits that the Tribunal, after considering the evidence available on record, has awarded just compensation, which needs no interference.

11. A perusal of the impugned order discloses that the Tribunal having framed issue No.1 as to whether the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, and having considered the evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documentary evidence i.e.,
Ex.A-1-FIR and Ex.A-4-charge-sheet, rightly held that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and has answered in favour of the petitioners and against the respondents.
Therefore, there are no reasons to interfere with the finding of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

12. Insofar as the quantum of compensation is concerned, though the petitioners stated that the deceased was earning Rs.7,500/- per month the Tribunal erroneously fixed the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.4,500/- per month.
Learned counsel for the petitioners stated that the Tribunal ought to have fixed the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.7,500/- per month.

In support of his contention, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners relied upon the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sanobanu Nazirbhai Mirza Vs. Ahmedabad Municipal Transport Service1 wherein it was held as under:

sentences.text:
"Having regard to nature of job that deceased was performing as skilled polisher, it would be just and proper to take his monthly income as Rs.5,000/- and adding 50%
towards future prospects and deducting 1/5th towards personal expenses, monthly income of deceased would come to Rs.6,000/-."

13. Learned counsel for the petitioners relied upon the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Arun Kumar 2014 (1) ALD 116 (SC) Agarwal Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd.2; Kirti vs. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.3 and Rajendra Singh vs. National Insurance Company Ltd.4 wherein the question involved was related to the fixation of income of housewife in the cases of motor accidents for the purpose of compensation and the Hon'ble Court found it appropriate to fix the same at Rs.5,000/-p.m.
14.

sentences.text: In the case on hand, the petitioners stated that the deceased was doing tailoring and embroidery work and earning Rs.7,500/- per month.
Though there is no evidence, the 1st petitioner on oath admitted the nature of the work done by the deceased i.e., tailoring and embroidery.

Therefore,
considering the nature of work done by the deceased and relying upon the above judgments, this Court is inclined to fix the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/- per month.
15. With regard to the multiplier, as per Exs.A-2 and A- 3- inquest and post-mortem reports, the age of the deceased was 23 years at the time of the accident.

As per Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation5, the appropriate multiplier 2 2010 (9) SCC 218 3 (2021) 2 SCC 166.
4 (2020) 7 SCC 256.
2009 ACJ 1208(SC) applicable for the age of the deceased is '18'.

entities.text: Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But, the Tribunal erroneously applied the multiplier '17' instead of '18'.
16. In the instant case, the monthly income of the deceased is fixed at Rs.5000/- per month.

Apart from the same, the petitioners are entitled to an addition of 40% towards future prospects on the income of the deceased, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others6.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others6
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.7,000/- (Rs.5,000/- + Rs.2,000/-).

From this, 1/4th is to be deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased following Sarla Verma's case (supra) as the petitioners are five in number and it would come to (Rs.7,000 - Rs.1,750) = Rs.5,250/- per month.
Thus, the annual income of the deceased comes to Rs.5,250 x 12 = Rs.63,000/-.
As the age of the deceased was 23 years at the time of the accident, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '18'.
Therefore, the total loss of dependency would come to Rs.11,34,000/- (Rs.63,000/- X 18).

The Tribunal granted a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.10,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.5,000/-
towards loss of consortium, 2017 ACJ 2700 which is meagre.
As per the decision of the Apex Court in Pranay Sethi's case (supra), the 1st petitioner, being the husband of the deceased, is entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- towards the spousal consortium.
The petitioners are further entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- (Rs.15,000/- + 10% + 15,000 + 10%) towards loss of estate and towards funeral expenses.
Thus, in all, the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.12,11,000/-.

Though the claimed amount is Rs.9,00,000/-, invoking the principle of just compensation, and in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajesh vs. Rajbir Singh7, and in a catena of decisions, this Court is empowered to grant compensation beyond the claimed amount.
18. Thus, the petitioners are entitled to the enhanced compensation of Rs.12,11,000/- as against the awarded amount of Rs.7,13,500/-.

19. Accordingly, the M.A.C.M.A is allowed, enhancing the compensation from Rs.7,13,500/- to Rs.12,11,000/- (Rupees Twelve lakh, eleven thousand only) with interest at the MANU/SC/0480/2013 rate of 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.

The respondents are directed to deposit the said amount, after giving due credit to the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
The compensation amount shall be apportioned among the petitioners in the same manner and ratio as ordered by the Tribunal.
However, the petitioners are directed to pay Deficit Court Fee on the enhanced amount within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any are pending, shall stand closed.

opennyai_summary.decision:
16. In the instant case, the monthly income of the deceased is fixed at Rs.5000/- per month.
Apart from the same, the petitioners are entitled to an addition of 40% towards future prospects on the income of the deceased, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others6.
Therefore, the monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.7,000/- (Rs.5,000/- + Rs.2,000/-).
From this, 1/4th is to be deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased following Sarla Verma's case (supra) as the petitioners are five in number and it would come to (Rs.7,000 - Rs.1,750) = Rs.5,250/- per month.
Thus, the annual income of the deceased comes to Rs.5,250 x 12 = Rs.63,000/-.
As the age of the deceased was 23 years at the time of the accident, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '18'.
Therefore, the total loss of dependency would come to Rs.11,34,000/- (Rs.63,000/- X 18).
The Tribunal granted a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.10,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.5,000/-
towards loss of consortium, 2017 ACJ 2700 which is meagre.
As per the decision of the Apex Court in Pranay Sethi's case (supra), the 1st petitioner, being the husband of the deceased, is entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- towards the spousal consortium.
The petitioners are further entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- (Rs.15,000/- + 10% + 15,000 + 10%) towards loss of estate and towards funeral expenses.
Thus, in all, the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.12,11,000/-.
18. Thus, the petitioners are entitled to the enhanced compensation of Rs.12,11,000/- as against the awarded amount of Rs.7,13,500/-.
19. Accordingly, the M.A.C.M.A is allowed, enhancing the compensation from Rs.7,13,500/- to Rs.12,11,000/- (Rupees Twelve lakh, eleven thousand only) with interest at the MANU/SC/0480/2013 rate of 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
The respondents are directed to deposit the said amount, after giving due credit to the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
The compensation amount shall be apportioned among the petitioners in the same manner and ratio as ordered by the Tribunal.
However, the petitioners are directed to pay Deficit Court Fee on the enhanced amount within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any are pending, shall stand closed.
